# llms-full.txt — Moran Zavdi — When Better Agent Behavior Does Not Improve Accuracy

Canonical site: https://aeterna-data-ai-ml-research.github.io/Kaggle-Gemma-4-Developer-Agent-Competition/
Canonical repo: https://github.com/Aeterna-Data-AI-ML-Research/Kaggle-Gemma-4-Developer-Agent-Competition
Kaggle competition: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent
Author: Moran Zavdi
License: Apache-2.0
Evidence cutoff: 2026-11-17

## One-sentence thesis
In autonomous software repair, shorter reasoning, earlier submission, and fewer timeouts can make an agent look operationally better without increasing the number of tasks it solves.

## Glossary
- D69: unadapted gemma-4-31b-it-qat-w4a16-ct baseline; public LB 0.18 (11/58 inferred).
- tr20: ForgeSWE rank-8 LoRA at adapter scale 2.0; public LB 0.17.
- scale10: same LoRA tensors at scale 1.0; public LB 0.13.
- P2_A / P2_B: clock-guard harness; clock-guard + pre-submit pytest gate.
- Think-1024: thinking_budget reduced from 4096 to 1024 on tr20 seed 1.
- WT (working-tree pass): final git working tree passes hidden tests (primary metric).
- Strict pass: WT pass and explicit submit_patch.
- Virtual clock: tokens/tok_per_sec + tool wall time; hard cutoff 420s.

## Experiment totals
- Phase 1 calibration: 900 episodes (3 arms × 2 seeds × 150 tasks)
- Phase 2 guards: 300 episodes
- Phase 3 thinking cap: 150 episodes
- Total: 1,350 controlled episodes

## Phase 1 WT results (pinned)
- D69: 93/300 = 31.0% (strict 58/300 = 19.3%)
- tr20 seed 0: 47/150 = 31.3% (strict 27/150)
- tr20 seed 1: 48/150 = 32.0% (strict 22/150)
- scale10: 91/300 = 30.3% (strict 47/300)
- Paired CIs vs D69 all include 0.

## Phase 3 Think-1024 (pinned)
- WT 48/150 vs baseline 48/150; flips +9/−9; CI includes 0.
- thoughts>1024: 3 vs 63; time_budget endings 77 vs 85; submitted 45 vs 34.
